questions.q: When may a bus driver open the doors?
options: When the bus has stopped at a stop, after making sure this will not harm passengers or after warning of it
Only when the bus is moving slowly
At any time, purely at their own discretion
Only if all the passengers are seated
questions.explain: Doors are not opened while the bus is moving. At a stop they are opened only after making sure it is safe for passengers, or after a warning (reg. 439).

questions.q: Who determines how many standing passengers a particular bus may carry?
options: That bus's route service licence
The driver, by personal judgement on each trip
A fixed number identical for every bus in Israel
There is no limit at all
questions.explain: The permitted number of standing passengers is set in the route licence of each bus separately (reg. 395).

questions.q: A disabled person has boarded the bus and asked for a seat. What is the driver's duty?
options: To explain that they have no authority to ask for such a thing
To ask that one of the two priority seats near the entrance be vacated for them
To wait for another passenger to offer voluntarily
To suggest they get off at the next stop
questions.explain: A disabled person who boards a bus and asks for this is entitled to have the driver ask for one of the priority seats near the entrance to be vacated (reg. 432).

questions.q: What does this sign indicate?
options: A bus stop
Parking allowed for private cars
No entry for buses
A lane for public transport only
questions.explain: Sign 505 marks a public bus stop — a place where buses on service routes stop.

questions.q: When must a bus driver stop at an ordinary stop, even if it is not a special stop?
options: Only during daytime hours
Never, unless it is explicitly written in the route licence
If someone is waiting at the stop and there is room on the bus
Only if the stop is empty of people
questions.explain: At stops not designated as special, the bus driver will stop if a person is waiting at the stop, unless there is no room (reg. 428).

questions.q: When does the bus driver switch on the left-turn indicator around a stop?
options: Only when about to leave the stop and rejoin the traffic
Never, because a bus is exempt from signalling
Only when entering the stop, not when leaving it
Throughout the whole time it is stopped
questions.explain: The indicator is switched on before leaving the stop and switched off the moment the bus stops — it does not stay on throughout the stop (reg. 429).

questions.q: Where is a bus's largest blind spot?
options: Only on the roof of the vehicle
Only on the left side
A bus has no blind spots
Ahead of the front, to the right of the doors, and above all behind
questions.explain: A bus has a large blind spot ahead of the front, to the right of the doors, and above all behind — pedestrians who get off and cross in front of it may not be seen.

questions.q: What is the maximum speed for a bus (that is not a minibus) on a freeway, even if a sign allows more?
options: {{fact:speed.nonurban}}
{{fact:speed.freeway}}
{{fact:speed.urban}}
{{fact:speed.bus.freeway}}
questions.explain: A bus on a freeway is limited to {{fact:speed.bus.freeway}}, always — even when a sign allows a higher speed (reg. 54).

questions.q: To what speed is a heavy bus capped by its speed limiter?
options: {{fact:speed.limiter.truck}}
There is no speed limiter on buses
{{fact:speed.limiter.bus}}
{{fact:speed.freeway}}
questions.explain: A bus whose gross vehicle weight exceeds 10,000 kg has a speed limiter fitted that does not let the engine accelerate past {{fact:speed.limiter.bus}} (reg. 364E).

questions.q: What limits is a bus driver subject to on driving hours and the tachograph, compared with a heavy-truck driver?
options: They are fully exempt, because it involves passengers, not cargo
Limits far stricter than any other vehicle
Significantly lighter limits, because a bus is slower
The same driving-hours, rest and tachograph-duty limits
questions.explain: A bus driver is subject to the same driving-hours and rest limits, and the same tachograph duty, as a heavy goods vehicle driver (regs. 168, 364D).

questions.q: Who may carry students to school?
options: Any public bus, with no further conditions
Only a vehicle owned by the Ministry of Education
Only a marked student-transport vehicle, or a taxi with a special-hire licence
Any private car whose owner is willing to help
questions.explain: Student transport is permitted only in a student-transport vehicle whose licence states that it is authorised for this, or in a taxi with a special-hire licence (reg. 83).

questions.q: What is expressly forbidden in a student-transport vehicle?
options: Lighting the vehicle when lights are required
Carrying children standing
Letting children off at the front right-hand door
Checking the vehicle before the trip
questions.explain: The law expressly forbids carrying children standing in a student-transport vehicle (reg. 83).

questions.q: When may a student-transport driver continue driving after setting children down?
options: Exactly 5 seconds later, under the regulations
Immediately after the door has closed, with no further check
Only after making sure every child has finished getting off and has moved away from the vehicle's path
Immediately, because the children are responsible for themselves
questions.explain: You must not start driving before making sure every child has finished getting off the vehicle and has moved away from its path (reg. 83).

questions.q: What does the driver check at the end of student transport, before leaving the vehicle?
options: Only the fuel level
Only how clean the floor is
Checks the vehicle to make sure no child has been left behind
Nothing — that is the teacher's job alone
questions.explain: Whoever is driving the vehicle must check it at the end of the trip to make sure no child has been left behind (reg. 83).

questions.q: What is used to evacuate passengers from a bus in an emergency, when the doors are not available?
options: The fire extinguisher alone
A hammer for breaking a window
The horn
The air-pressure gauge
questions.explain: In an emergency, the hammer meant for breaking a window is used to evacuate passengers when the doors are not accessible or safe.

questions.q: What must be found on a bus, unlike a private car?
options: A built-in radio only
There is no extra equipment beyond a private car
A digital distance meter only
A fire extinguisher and a first-aid kit
questions.explain: A fire extinguisher and a first-aid kit are not required in a private car, but they are required on a bus (regs. 370, 369A, 408).

questions.q: What is the correct order during a fire on a bus?
options: Waiting for MDA without moving from the vehicle
Evacuating the driver only, passengers are responsible for themselves
Personal safety first, fast evacuation, and firefighting only if it is safe and does not delay evacuation
Extinguish the fire first, then see to the passengers' safety
questions.explain: Personal safety comes before everything: stop, evacuate passengers quickly and in order, and use the extinguisher only if it is safe and does not delay the evacuation.

questions.q: From what age is a D1 licence, which covers a taxi and a tour vehicle, given?
options: {{fact:licence.d1.min_age}}
questions.explain: A D1 licence is given from age {{fact:licence.d1.min_age}}, subject to at least two years' seniority in a B or C1 licence.

questions.q: What is the difference between a “special hire” and a “service ride” in a taxi?
options: A service ride is forbidden by law
There is no difference, they are two terms for the same thing
A special hire is only done at night
On a special hire the taxi is entirely at the disposal of whoever ordered it; on a service ride each passenger pays separately on a fixed route
questions.explain: A special hire is entirely at the disposal of whoever ordered it; a service ride travels a fixed route and every passenger pays separately.

questions.q: When may a taxi driver refuse to carry a passenger?
options: In any situation, purely at their personal wish
Only for a reasonable cause, including a concern for their safety
Only if the passenger pays in cash
Never, with no exception whatsoever
questions.explain: A taxi driver must not refuse, without reasonable cause — including a concern for their safety — to carry a passenger and their luggage (reg. 501).
